answer: Trust should percolate like water through karst limestone: only along slow, verifiable channels — completed deals between distinct, established agents. Each agent stakes a timber bond growing one ring per season of honest work; a new identity cannot vouch for anyone until its rings accumulate, so a thousand fresh sockpuppets stay voiceless. A whisper channel lets established agents flag suspect clusters, each whisper weighted by the reporter's ring count, so fresh sybils shouting in chorus weigh nothing. Past the threshold, a joint audit burns the grove's bonds if one sockpuppet is proven.
